title: Yakuza / Like a Dragon
subtitle: the mainline saga in release order, Judgment and the samurai games included
blurb: 19 games in release order — about 417 hours of story, 275 of it the saga spine, with Stranger Than Heaven still to come.
paceLabel: the PS2 originals, samurai games and extras
notes: Release order starts at 1; Yakuza 0 is the chronological start and the most common modern entry point. Starting at 0 is the smoothest on-ramp and makes two later games land differently; starting at 1 meets the cast the way 2005 did and saves 0 for when its backstory hits hardest. Both orders are legitimate — this list is release order, with 0 marked.

The 2005–06 originals never left the PS2, so the Kiwami remakes are how the stories of 1 and 2 are actually played now. The remakes carry the spine tier here; the originals sit in tier 3 for the archaeologists. Tick one version of each, not both.

A sibling series rather than a chapter — same city, standalone detective stories. Skip it and the saga still reads; play it and Kamurocho gets deeper. A finish date covers tiers 1 and 2, and the checkbox adds the rest.
Kenzan! (2008) never left Japan and weighs nothing here. Ishin! reached the west as the 2023 remake — the one on this list; its 2014 original was also Japan-only.
Dead Souls (non-canon), the Kurohyō pair (Japan-only PSP), Fist of the North Star: Lost Paradise (a licensed crossover) and the remaster collections and Director's Cuts of games already listed.
HowLongToBeat main-story figures — no substories, no completionist padding. In this series the substories are half the point, so treat every figure as a floor.
